content:
Both lines pass through the center \((a,1)\), and their slopes are \(-\frac12\) and \(2\), so they are perpendicular. Thus they are perpendicular diameters of the circle of radius \(2\).

The quadrilateral formed by the four intersection points has diagonals of length \(4\) and \(4\), perpendicular to each other.

\[
\text{Area}=\frac12(4)(4)=8
\]

\[
\boxed{8}
\]
